records.title: FIRST WORLD AIDS DAY
records.summary: The first World AIDS Day was observed worldwide to raise awareness, encourage solidarity with people living with HIV, and remember those who had died from AIDS-related illnesses.

records.title: ATLANTIS LAUNCHES ON STS-27
records.summary: Space Shuttle Atlantis launched from Kennedy Space Center at 9:30:34 a.m. EST on a classified Department of Defense mission with five astronauts aboard.

records.title: PIONEER VENUS ORBITER MARKS TEN YEARS
records.summary: NASA's Pioneer Venus Orbiter marked ten years studying Venus from orbit, an unusually long planetary mission for its era.

records.title: STS-27 RETURNS TO EARTH
records.summary: Atlantis landed at Edwards Air Force Base after 68 orbits and a mission lasting four days, nine hours, five minutes, and 37 seconds.

records.title: DESTRUCTIVE EARTHQUAKE STRIKES ARMENIA
records.summary: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck northern Armenia near Spitak at 07:41 UTC, causing catastrophic destruction and a major international relief effort.

records.title: GORBACHEV ADDRESSES THE UNITED NATIONS
records.summary: Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev addressed the United Nations General Assembly in New York during its 43rd session and discussed international security and reductions in armed forces.
records.source: United Nations General Assembly official record

records.title: 1988 NOBEL PRIZES PRESENTED
records.summary: The year's Nobel laureates received their awards in Stockholm and Oslo on Nobel Day, the anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death.

records.title: CLAPHAM JUNCTION RAIL COLLISION
records.summary: A railway collision near Clapham Junction in London killed 35 people and injured 484. The subsequent inquiry drove major changes in British railway signalling safety.

records.title: NETWORK BOOT PROTOCOL WORK CONTINUES
records.summary: During December 1988, Internet engineers published RFC 1084 describing BOOTP vendor information extensions. The Internet remained primarily a research and institutional network, separate from commercial dial-up services.

records.title: PAN AM FLIGHT 103 DESTROYED OVER LOCKERBIE
records.summary: A bomb destroyed Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, killing all 259 people aboard and 11 people on the ground. The investigation became a major international effort.

records.title: CHICO MENDES KILLED IN BRAZIL
records.summary: Rubber-tapper union leader and environmental activist Chico Mendes was murdered in Xapuri, Acre, after campaigning for workers' rights and preservation of the Amazon forest.

records.title: THE DIAL-UP ONLINE WORLD
records.summary: As 1988 closed, most home users reached commercial information services and bulletin-board systems by modem. These systems offered mail, forums, files, news, and databases but were generally separate from the Internet.
records.source: Period context prepared for this simulation

records.title: ATLANTIS CREW INSPECTS TILE DAMAGE
records.summary: During STS-27, the crew used the shuttle's robot arm and camera to inspect damage to thermal-protection tiles on Atlantis. The classified communications link made the imagery difficult for controllers to assess.

records.title: MODEMS CONNECT HOME COMPUTERS
records.summary: A typical home online session in 1988 used an acoustic or direct-connect modem at 300, 1200, or increasingly 2400 baud. Long sessions could incur both service and telephone charges.
records.source: Period context prepared for this simulation

records.title: REAGAN HOLDS HIS FINAL FORMAL NEWS CONFERENCE
records.summary: President Ronald Reagan held the final formal news conference of his presidency as the transition to President-elect George H. W. Bush continued.
records.source: Ronald Reagan Presidential Library audiovisual archives

records.title: FRENCH-SOVIET CREW WORKS OUTSIDE MIR
records.summary: Cosmonauts Vladimir Titov and Jean-Loup Chretien conducted an extravehicular activity outside the Mir space station during the joint Soviet-French Aragatz mission.

records.title: RELIEF AIRCRAFT CRASHES IN ARMENIA
records.summary: An Ilyushin Il-76 carrying personnel for the Armenian earthquake relief effort crashed near Leninakan, adding another tragedy to the continuing emergency response.

records.title: SOUTHERN AFRICA PEACE NEGOTIATIONS
records.summary: Diplomats from Angola, Cuba, South Africa, the United States, and the Soviet Union were completing negotiations that would produce the December 22 Tripartite Accord and a path toward Namibian independence.

records.title: GENERAL STRIKE IN SPAIN
records.summary: Spanish trade unions staged a nationwide general strike that halted much transport, broadcasting, and industrial activity while challenging the government's economic and labor policies.

records.title: RAIN MAN OPENS IN THE UNITED STATES
records.summary: Rain Man, starring Dustin Hoffman and Tom Cruise, entered theatrical release. It later received Academy Awards including Best Picture and Best Actor.

records.title: THE 80386 AT THE HIGH END
records.summary: Computers built around Intel's 80386 processor represented the high end of the personal-computer market. Many home and office systems still used 8088, 8086, or 80286 processors.
records.source: Period context prepared for this simulation

records.title: ELECTRONIC MAIL BEFORE THE WEB
records.summary: Electronic mail existed on commercial online services, corporate networks, universities, and the Internet, but addresses and gateways varied. The World Wide Web had not yet been proposed.
records.source: Period context prepared for this simulation

records.title: SRI LANKA HOLDS PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION
records.summary: Sri Lanka held a presidential election in a period marked by civil conflict and political violence. Ranasinghe Premadasa was elected president.

records.title: TEXT INFORMATION MOVES BY MODEM
records.summary: Before graphical web browsers, online information was commonly read as terminal text. Capturing a session to disk allowed members to disconnect and read material without accumulating connect-time charges.
records.source: Period context prepared for this simulation

records.title: TANKER EXPLOSION IN MEMPHIS
records.summary: A propane tanker crashed and exploded at an interstate interchange in Memphis, Tennessee. The fire and secondary accidents killed motorists and nearby residents.

records.title: HOLIDAY MESSAGES CROSS ONLINE SERVICES
records.summary: Online mail and bulletin-board messages offered computer users a fast way to exchange holiday greetings, although many recipients would not see a message until their next dial-up session.
records.source: Period context prepared for this simulation

records.title: A HOME-COMPUTER CHRISTMAS
records.summary: Personal computers, game systems, printers, modems, and software were prominent technology purchases in the late 1980s. Installation often meant consulting printed manuals and configuring hardware switches or DOS files.
records.source: Period context prepared for this simulation

records.title: ARMENIAN RELIEF CONTINUES
records.summary: International rescue, medical, shelter, and reconstruction work continued after the December 7 Armenian earthquake, under difficult winter conditions and amid immense damage.

records.title: FERRY DISASTER IN BANGLADESH
records.summary: A crowded passenger ferry sank in Bangladesh, one of several severe disasters affecting the country during the closing weeks of 1988.

records.title: UNITED STATES EXTENDS TERRITORIAL SEA
records.summary: President Reagan proclaimed a 12-nautical-mile territorial sea for the United States, extending the previous three-nautical-mile claim while preserving navigation rights.

records.title: INTERNET HOST REQUIREMENTS ARE REVIEWED
records.summary: Internet engineers were consolidating and reviewing host requirements that would soon appear as RFC 1122 and RFC 1123. Standards work circulated through RFC documents rather than the later web.
records.source: RFC Editor history of the RFC series

records.title: YUGOSLAV FEDERAL GOVERNMENT RESIGNS
records.summary: Yugoslav Prime Minister Branko Mikulic and his federal cabinet resigned amid economic crisis and disputes over austerity and constitutional change.
